subject: Clarify: Incident notification lifecycle & subprocessor access for telemetry exposures
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <security@fintrust.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@fintrust.com
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry exposure — notice window and subprocessor access

Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. We flagged a non-customer telemetry exposure in our environment that may include metadata routed through Redwood's ingestion pipeline. Our counsel asked for clarity on the contractual notification path and what evidence we can expect from Redwood if this elevates. Specifically:

- Confirmation of notification windows by severity (what you consider Critical / High / Moderate and the corresponding SLA).
- What artifacts you can provide (telemetry snapshots, server timestamps, delivery logs, anonymized payload examples).
- Whether Redwood can provide subprocessor forensic snapshots or if you require a legal process / SFTP access for transfers.
- Cross-border constraints: if evidence contains EU-origin telemetry, how does Redwood handle export/consent?

We're hoping for a concise matrix so we can align with our incident response timeline and upstream notifications to regulators. Can someone from your security/compliance team loop in the format and typical delivery timelines?

Appreciate it — Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Security Operations, FinTrust
[attachment: incident_alert_summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <security@fintrust.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry exposure — notice window and subprocessor access

Alyssa — thanks for the heads up and sorry to hear you hit this. I put together a proposed operational mapping attached (incident-lifecycle-matrix.xlsx) and a short checklist for subprocessor access. High level answers below; please treat this as our proposed default and we'll flag exceptions based on legal/contractual constraints.

Proposed notice windows by impact class (examples):
- Critical (active data exfiltration / PII confirmed): initial notification within 24 hours, substantive update + evidence package within 72 hours.
- High (sensitive telemetry with potential user-identifiers): initial notification within 48 hours, evidence package within 7 days.
- Moderate (non-sensitive telemetry anomaly): notification within 7 days, summary report within 14 days.

Typical evidence we can provide (subject to crossborder/export and legal constraints):
- Delivery logs & timestamps (CSV)
- Aggregated telemetry samples (anonymized)
- Forensic snapshots (available for dedicated customers or under a signed SFTP/evidence transfer agreement)
- KV cache traces and request IDs to correlate events

Subprocessor access: we can do one of the following depending on customer comfort and DPA terms:
1) Direct handoff: Redwood prepares a redacted forensic snapshot and uploads to an SFTP/secure share (preferred).
2) On-site/partner-assisted export: we coordinate with a forensic vendor under an NDA and provide scoped exports.
3) Legal process: for subpoenas or regulatory demands we require proper legal docs before full raw exports.

Cross-border: for EU-origin data we follow the DPA export controls — we attempt to produce redacted evidence without export if possible; if raw extracts are required, we route through our EU data-onshore process or require customer consent when feasible.

I've looped Marissa (legal) and Ben (security) to confirm these are acceptable and to flag any DPA/contractual limits. See attachments for the matrix and the checklist.

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Alyssa Chen <security@fintrust.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry exposure — notice window and subprocessor access

Thanks — this is a solid starting point. Quick legal notes:
- Our standard DPA (§5.3) requires "prompt" notification; for enterprise deals we often agree specific hour windows as SLOs. We should avoid committing beyond our Hosted API policy for non-dedicated customers.
- Forensic snapshots: we can agree to provide redacted exports under a signed evidence-transfer addendum (DocuSign link below). Full raw access will need either (a) the customer to be on Dedicated, or (b) a narrow legal order.

Action items:
- Ben: confirm operational feasibility of 24h initial notice + 72h evidence package for Critical on Hosted tenants (do we have automation for delivery logs?).
- Kar​t​hik: confirm whether FinTrust is on Dedicated or Hosted; that determines whether we can give full snapshots. Alyssa — can you confirm their purchase model?
- Marissa: I'll draft the short addendum language for subproc evidence transfer and circulate a redline.

DocuSign draft for evidence-transfer addendum: https://www.docusign.com/link/FT-47-evidence-addendum

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Counsel, Privacy & Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <security@fintrust.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry exposure — notice window and subprocessor access

Alyssa — quick operational reply from infra/security side:
- We can reliably produce delivery logs + anonymized telemetry samples within 48 hours for Hosted accounts via our incident-export job. For Critical incidents we'll prioritize a 24-hour initial shim (meta-report) and push a full package within 72 hours if the tenant is Dedicated; otherwise 72 hours for initial package is aggressive but possible with additional manual triage.
- If FinTrust wants a full forensic snapshot and they are on Hosted, we will require the evidence-transfer addendum + an SFTP endpoint. For Dedicated accounts we can provide a scoped snapshot under the customer's access controls.
- Cross-border: logs with EU subject-matter require redaction unless customer consents. If you need a raw EU-origin payload for regulatory reasons, we'll need to run the export through our EU onshore process (adds ~48-72 hours).

Next steps: Alyssa — if you confirm FinTrust's tenancy and whether you want the DocuSign addendum executed, we'll queue the incident-export job and schedule a handoff call with our forensics partner.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
